edition.intro: This week's edit is about wearing more of what you already own: clear out the closet, then add a few fall pieces in brown, velvet, animal print, and good shoes.

items.snippet: Read this if you want to start getting your closet ready for 2027 now.
items.headline: How to Clean Out Your Closet Without Losing Your Mind
items.summary: Professional organizers and a stylist say you shouldn't empty the whole closet at once, and several of them are done with the "haven't worn it in a year" rule. Their advice is to work one category at a time, edit before you organize, and be honest about duplicates of basics. Replace worn-out everyday items, and get quality coats and blazers repaired or tailored.
items.tip: Pick one category, such as shoes or sweaters, and edit just that this week.

items.title: Ask Earl With Laurel Pantin: How to Style Leopard as a Neutral
items.snippet: In her monthly column, Ask Earl, writer, editor, mom, and entrepreneur, Laurel Pantin answers your latest style questions.
items.headline: How to Style Leopard Print as a Neutral
items.summary: A stylist explains that animal print works like a neutral because its colors are earthy and the pattern is so familiar. To keep it from looking costume-y, she mixes in casual pieces like sweatshirts and denim, and adds a bit of humor or a slightly odd accessory. Bright red and tonal browns also work well alongside it.
items.tip: Wear your leopard piece with dark jeans or a sweatshirt to make it feel like everyday dressing.

items.title: Brown Midiskirts That'll Go With Every Shoe in Your Closet This Fall
items.snippet: It's rare to find a piece that works with heels, boots, and sneakers.
items.headline: Brown Midiskirts Are the Fall Piece That Goes With Every Shoe
items.summary: A brown midiskirt can be a calm base for bright colors or the star of an all-brown outfit. It works with heels, loafers, ballet flats, and even sneakers. Black on top and brown below is a particularly current combination.
items.tip: Try a brown midiskirt with a black top and the flats or loafers you already own.

items.title: The ‘Imperfect Manicure’ Trend Is Finally Making Smudged Nail Polish Cool
items.snippet: The manicure “even your boyfriend could have done.”
items.headline: The Imperfect Manicure Makes Smudges Cool
items.summary: Messy, haphazardly applied nail polish appeared at a recent Paris runway show and is catching on for fall. Unlike the Brazilian manicure, the stray polish isn't cleaned up. The idea is a relaxed rejection of perfectionism, so a less-than-flawless manicure doesn't need fixing.
items.tip: Skip the cleanup on your next at-home manicure and enjoy the imperfect result.

items.title: No Need To Guess—6 Fall Shoe Trends Fashion People Are Wearing Right Now
items.snippet: From animal print to penny loafers.
items.headline: Six Fall Shoe Trends Worth Knowing
items.summary: This season's footwear leans toward animal prints, jewel-toned colors, tall boots with pointed or square toes, and ballet pumps with a small heel. Sleek penny loafers are replacing chunky soles, and elegant slipper-style shoes are also showing up. You don't need all of them, because one well-chosen pair can refresh a lot of outfits.
items.tip: Choose one shoe trend that suits what you already wear and shop only for that.

items.title: How to Wear Velvet Pants, According to the Runways
items.snippet: From Burberry’s utilitarian twist to Tory Burch’s stripes, the runways make the case for wearing velvet pants every day.
items.headline: Velvet Pants Are Now an Everyday Trouser
items.summary: Velvet is no longer just for holiday parties, as designers showed it styled casually and in tailored ways. Treat velvet pants like any other trouser, with a fine knit, a white shirt, or a blazer, and keep accessories simple because the fabric already stands out. Loafers make them daytime-friendly, and heels with a silk blouse take them to evening.
items.tip: Wear velvet pants with a plain knit and flats on a regular weekday.

practice: Putting it into practice: start by shopping your closet, one category at a time. Pull out your skirts, trousers, and shoes, and keep only what fits, feels like you, and gets worn. Check that leopard piece, any velvet, and your best boots or loafers, and have good coats or blazers repaired or tailored rather than replaced. Replace only the basics that have truly worn out.

If you're buying something, pick one item that works with several things you own, such as a brown midiskirt or a pair of velvet trousers. Wear the skirt with black knitwear and flats, or wear velvet with a simple sweater and loafers. Mix in your leopard accessory or jeans for an easy, casual finish, and don't stress about perfect nails.
